name: Latium and Roma
note: The capital receives the complete layered portfolio as the empire's exceptional fiscal consumption and redistribution centre.

name: Northern Italian Cities
note: Urban and agricultural northern Italy emphasizes roads grain building materials textiles and metal craft.

name: Upper Adriatic Corridor
note: Adriatic markets combine river and sea logistics with frontier supply and urban craft.

name: Southern Italian Ports
note: Southern ports emphasize oil wine ceramics maritime redistribution and mixed Hellenic civic life.

name: Baetican Export Cities
note: Baetican cities emphasize oil wine amphora supply metals and Atlantic-Mediterranean export handling.

name: Tarraconensian Corridor
note: The provincial corridor combines road supply civic building and mixed agricultural craft.

name: Lusitanian Atlantic Cities
note: Atlantic and inland capital proxies emphasize roads river trade stone metal and agricultural processing without asserting quantified exports.

name: Narbonensian Markets
note: Narbonensian cities combine Rhone and Mediterranean exchange with wine oil ceramics and civic display.

name: Lugdunensis and Aquitania
note: River markets emphasize transport provisioning textiles pottery and the supply of the northern provinces.

name: Africa Proconsularis
note: African cities emphasize grain oil ceramics ports and the infrastructure of Roman urban consumption.

name: African Coastal Frontier
note: The profile models a thinner coastal and frontier logistics layer rather than equal metropolitan development.

name: Aegyptus
note: Alexandria emphasizes annona handling papyrus-linked urban craft maritime exchange and monumental water-dependent density.

name: Achaia
note: Corinth combines port exchange craft quarters sanctuaries and Roman colonial civic investment.

name: Asia Province
note: Ephesus emphasizes port commerce dense civic infrastructure textiles ceramics and regional luxury processing.

name: Syria Province
note: Antioch combines long-distance exchange frontier supply monumental water systems and a dense craft economy.
